Subject: Post-call: Long-window evaluation fit & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Priya — helpful to understand the discharge-summary and longitudinal-visit use cases. Short recap and suggested next steps below so we can align on scope and get a pilot started quickly.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary need: accurate visit-history summarization that preserves critical findings buried late in multi-visit notes (10–40k tokens).
- Failure mode observed: truncation causes missing last-visit diagnoses; summarization sometimes hallucinates or omits medication changes.
- Success metric: end-to-end fidelity measured on an annotated set (precision/recall for extracted clinical facts) plus human evals for comprehensiveness.

Initial model-fit recommendations (to evaluate)
1) Redwood Long-32k-v1 (our long-context variant) — baseline for fidelity across long histories.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B-8k (cost-efficient candidate) + prefix-KV caching to keep recent visits in cache.
3) Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized) for a higher-coverage run when latency/cost are acceptable.

Planned benchmarks and tests
- Truncation stress test: synthetic documents with critical items in final 5% of tokens.
- Summarization fidelity: ROUGE + targeted clinical fact checklist (med changes, diagnoses, pending labs).
- Regression checks: compare outputs to your golden set and track hallucination rate per model.

Attachments I uploaded for you: healthnote-sample-patient-rows.csv (anonymized rows), long-window-benchmark-spec.md (test descriptions + expected outputs).

Next steps (action items)
- Priya: confirm we can run on the anonymized sample file above or provide a small additional sample (5–10 patient histories) — target by Tue EOD.
- Priya/Alex: decide if we want to scope a narrow pilot (summarize last 3 visits) vs full history pilot.
- Neha/Marissa: draft pilot SOW and a 4-week eval plan (I'll leave technical acceptance criteria to you).

If that looks right I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Tuesday to lock scope and access.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Priya — great questions, answers below and I added concrete acceptance criteria so the pilot can be signed off.

1) Sliding windows vs prefix caching
- Sliding window: we chunk the document into overlapping windows and run summary passes; good for bounded memory but can lose cross-window references.
- Prefix/KV caching: recommended for your use case — we keep KV state for the last N tokens (recent visits) so the model has direct access to recent context without re-tokenizing everything. For very long histories we combine both: a compressed summary of older history + KV cache for the last ~8k tokens.

2) Latency expectations
- Long-32k-v1 (32k context): median token generation ~0.9–1.6s per token depending on concurrency; for 2k output summaries expect end-to-end 18–40s in our hosted tests.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-8k: median ~0.15–0.4s per token, so 2k summary ~3–8s.
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized): median ~0.6–1.1s per token; 2k summary ~12–25s.

Suggested pilot acceptance criteria
- Fidelity: >= 92% recall on the clinical fact checklist for the 5 patient benchmark.
- No critical truncation failures: at least 95% of cases must preserve the final-visit diagnosis.
- Hallucination rate: <= 4% false clinical facts in slice-reviewed outputs.

3) Security/deployment
- We can run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated in us-east region; I'll loop in our Security AE to provide the pilot checklist and a short Dedicated onboarding doc.

I'll schedule the 30-min kickoff for Tue 4/13 10:00 AM ET (if that works for your team). Neha/Marissa — please draft the SOW + pilot timeline (4 weeks) and attach the Dedicated checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik
